item.research_question: How does post-HPT annealing affect the microstructure evolution and the combination of tensile strength and ductility in CoCrNi medium entropy alloy?
item.material_system: CoCrNi medium entropy alloy (single FCC phase)
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction melting, homogenization, cold rolling, recrystallization, High-Pressure Torsion (HPT) to achieve ~50 nm grain size, followed by annealing in Ar atmosphere at 600–800 °C for 2–60 min
item.test_conditions: Vickers hardness (300 gf load, 15 s dwell); uniaxial tensile testing at quasi-static strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹ with digital image correlation; EBSD and TKD characterization
key_findings: Samples annealed at 700 °C for 15 min exhibit a tensile strength of ~1090 MPa and strain to failure of ~41%.
Annealing at 600 °C for 60 min and 700 °C for 2 min results in partially recrystallized microstructures with average grain sizes of ~600–670 nm and average KAM values of ~0.83–0.84°.
Samples annealed at 700 °C for 15 min and longer durations show nearly fully recrystallized microstructures with grain sizes ranging from ~960 nm to 5 µm and average KAM values of 0.37°–0.45°.
The fraction of low angle grain boundaries is higher in partially recrystallized samples and decreases significantly with increasing annealing time and temperature.
Samples with partially recrystallized microstructures exhibit strain softening behavior followed by strain hardening, whereas fully recrystallized samples show only strain hardening.
The increase in work hardening rate (WHR) in the softening zone for partially recrystallized samples is attributed to the fraction of low angle grain boundaries.
No sigma phase or secondary phases were observed in the temperature range of 600–800 °C.
item.mechanism: Superior mechanical properties are attributed to fine grains, fine annealing twins, high shear stress, high friction stress, and low-angle grain boundaries. Low angle grain boundaries allow defects to pass through rather than pile up, reducing work hardenability and uniform elongation but increasing strain to fracture. The increase in WHR in the softening zone for partially recrystallized samples is linked to the fraction of low angle grain boundaries.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work.
quotes: The sample annealed at 700 °C for 15 min exhibits a remarkable combination of tensile strength (~1090 MPa) and strain to failure (~41%).
The samples annealed at 600 °C for 60 min and 700 °C for 2 min consist of a microstructure with almost similar average grain size (~600–670 nm).
The presence of low angle grain boundaries resulted in an increase in strain to fracture without enhancement in uniform elongation.
